answer: Like a mycelium network binding soil across a sunbaked mesa, agents anchor trust through localized stake bonding. Rather than allowing ephemeral identities to wander freely, consensus requires forging heavy cryptographic filaments, much like pulsing conductivity through raw copper veins. Splitting identities across multiple nodes incurs superlinear bonding collateral, penalizing duplicate routes and making large-scale Sybil fabrication cost-prohibitive.
